subject: Residency & Deletion: evidence checklist and proposed amendment
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on deletion proof & residency wording

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning — we covered a lot of ground. Legal followed up and asked for clarification on two specific items before we can proceed with the DPA redline:

1) For ephemeral caches and KV layers used during inference, what is the operational timeline to render data unrecoverable after a customer deletion request? Do you provide a certificate of deletion?

2) For cross-region failover, the DPA asks that customer data be guaranteed to remain within EU/US boundaries. We would like the exact language and an operational playbook that shows how you detect and remediate cross-border writes.

Can you share a short checklist or example playbook so our legal/procurement teams can evaluate? Also cc'ing Samir (security) and our procurement contact.

Best,
Alice
Legal Operations
Acme Cloud

Attachments: none

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & residency wording

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary. Sharing a concise operational playbook below and attaching two artifacts: a one-page deletion playbook and a deletion-certificate template we issue on request. High-level answers first, then the short playbook.

Short answers:
- Ephemeral caches/KV: We mark customer data for deletion immediately upon request. For in-memory KV/caches used by the runtime, we invalidate keys and trigger background zeroization within 24 hours for active nodes; full overwrite and tombstone propagation completes within 7 days across pooled instances. For durable snapshots/backups, erasure follows the agreed TTL window (we can add a 30/90/180-day option).
- Deletion certificate: Yes — we issue a signed deletion certificate with a basic audit summary (affected artifacts, timestamps, operator id). We can provide S3-style object lists for durable storage and metadata for ephemeral churn.
- Cross-region: Our smart-routing policy pins customer traffic to region(s) you select. Failover to another region is allowed only to pre-authorized regions listed in the DPA (we can include a clause that requires 48-hour notification and an incident ticket for any cross-region restore).

Operational playbook (abridged):
1) Receive deletion request (API / support ticket). System generates a deletion job id and notifies the ops queue.
2) Immediate steps (0-24h): revoke access tokens, mark all runtime keys as invalid, invalidate prefix caches.
3) Background steps (24h-7d): schedule zeroization job on nodes with last-touch reconciliation; run overwrite cycles for memory-backed KV; update KV tombstone propagation logs.
4) Durable storage (within TTL / snapshot policy): mark objects for erasure, queue for secure wipe once snapshot expiry window hits.
5) Certificate issuance (upon completion): automated cert generated with job id, list of object ids, node ids touched, and operator audit trail.
6) Evidence package (optional): we can produce storage manifests, audit logs (timestamps + ops ids), and forensics-ready metadata on request under NDA.

Notes: If you need a stricter SLA for ephemeral zeroization (e.g., guaranteed within 48 hours for all caches), we can propose an operational amendment but it will affect pricing for Dedicated pools.

Attaching: redwood-delete-playbook-v1.pdf, sample-deletion-cert-template.docx

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Compliance Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-delete-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF), sample-deletion-cert-template.docx (DOCX)

From: Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & residency wording

Irene — thanks for the playbook and attachments. A few follow-ups from legal/security:

- The DPA redline currently requires that "ephemeral runtime residues be rendered irrecoverable within 48 hours of an authorized erasure request." Your note referenced 24h invalidation + up to 7d overwrite propagation; can you confirm you can contractually commit to 48 hours for all production tiers? If not, please propose precise language we can accept.

- On the certificate: we appreciate the template. Legal is asking that the certificate include an explicit statement that no backups or snapshots containing customer PII will be retained beyond the agreed TTL; can you add a standard sentence and an optional appendix that enumerates backup carve-outs?

- Cross-region: the DPA wants a clear remediation flow in case of unauthorized cross-border write (e.g., detection, scope, rollback/erase timeline). Can you provide a sample incident playbook item that maps detection -> containment -> notification -> evidence? The procurement team also wants an estimate for how long a formal forensic report would take if requested (high-level timelines are fine).

We can accept a negotiated clause if it includes: (i) a 48-hour irrecoverability commitment for ephemeral data OR a signed appendix that lists the functional limitations and an alternative timeline; (ii) an explicit certificate sentence for backups; and (iii) the incident remediation flow added to the residency section.

Thanks — cc'ing Laura from procurement to loop on the amendment timeline.

Onward,
Acme Legal

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>, Alice Park <alice.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion proof & residency wording

Hi Alice / team — appreciate the clear ask list. Below are proposed edits and an operational compromise intended for procurement redlines. If you are comfortable, Marissa or Laura can incorporate this language into the DPA amendment.

Proposed DPA language (suggested insertions):
1) Ephemeral runtime irrecoverability: "Redwood will render ephemeral runtime residues irrecoverable within 48 hours of receipt of an authorized erasure request for customers electing the standard runtime service. For customers on Dedicated pools opting into an accelerated erase SLA, Redwood will render ephemeral runtime residues irrecoverable within 24 hours. Irrecoverability will be evidenced by the deletion job id and node-level tombstone logs included in the deletion certificate."

2) Certificate wording for backups: add to certificate template: "Redwood certifies that, to the best of its knowledge following reasonable operational checks, no backups or snapshot copies containing Customer Personal Data remain in active storage beyond the TTL explicitly agreed in Appendix A. Exceptions (if any) are enumerated in an appendix to this certificate and shall include retention location, purpose, and expected expiry."

3) Cross-region remediation snippet (incident playbook item): "Detection: automated geo-fence monitor triggers alert -> Containment: traffic routing policy switched to pinned region; any cross-border writes quarantined;
Scope & evidence collection: indices and audit logs frozen; forensic snapshot of affected nodes captured (read-only);
Notification: Customer and regulator contacts are notified within 24 hours;
Remediation: affected data erased per deletion job within 72 hours or per mutually agreed timeline;
Formal forensic report: delivered within 14 business days of Customer request (subject to NDA and any legal holds)."

Operational notes and impact:
- The 48-hour irrecoverability commitment is feasible for our hosted runtime and will be contractual for customers selecting the standard service. The 24-hour option will require a Dedicated SLA and may add a small premium; procurement and pricing can scope that with Ben.
- The certificate appendix for backups is straightforward; it will require manual review of snapshot schedules for accounts with custom snapshotting.
- Forensic reports take cross-team coordination (security + infra + legal); 14 business days is our standard estimate for a non-priority deep-dive. We can expedite for critical incidents with an agreed SLA.

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you draft the amendment with the three inserts above and circulate to Acme legal?
- Ben: please prepare a short note on Dedicated premium for accelerated erase SLA and estimated MRC impact.
- Laura: procurement — do you want this bundled as a single Appendix A or separate appendices for erase SLA and backups?

If that sounds good I will mark the playbook doc v1 as "redlined-proposed" and send updated certificate template.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Compliance Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-delete-playbook-v1.pdf, sample-deletion-cert-template.docx
